For the Petitioner : Mr. R.S. Mazumdar, Sr.

By the Court:-
1. Heard the parties.

2. This criminal miscellaneous petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 03.06.2023, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Dhanbad in Complaint Case No. 6913 of 2022 whereby and where under the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offence punishable under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioners and directed for issuance of summons.
3.

The allegation against the petitioners is that the complainant was having a showroom of Sonalika Brand of Tractors manufactured by the petitioner no.1-company and the billing of the showroom was closed by the petitioner no.1-company in June, 2019.

On 22.06.2022, the petitioner no.6 in furtherance of common intention with the petitioner no.5 induced the complainant to pay Rs.10,00,000/- in cash out of Rs.26,00,000/-; so that the dealership of the complainant will be restarted and the billing of five tractors will be made.

The complainant handed over Rs.10,00,000/- in cash at a hotel to the petitioner no.6 and the remaining Rs.16,00,000/-
was handed over by the complainant to the petitioner no.5 at Ranchi but they dishonestly misappropriated the said money and did not do the billing of the five tractors as promised by them.

On the basis of the complaint, statement of the complainant on solemn affirmation and the statement of the inquiry witnesses, the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Dhanbad found prima facie case for the offence punishable under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioners and directed for issuance of summons.

4. It is submitted by the learned senior counsel for the petitioners that there is absolutely no allegation against the petitioner nos. 1 to 4 of having played any role in the whole occurrence and the allegation is confined only to the petitioner nos. 5 & 6.
It is then submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are false.

It is next submitted by the learned senior counsel for the petitioners Tractors Ltd vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128511123/
2 that the petitioner no.1 terminated the dealership of the complainant and allowed another dealer for the district of Dumka in the year 2019.

sentences.text: The complainant kept pursuing the petitioner no.5 for grant of dealership in any area of Jharkhand, if not in his name, then in the name of his younger brother but as the dealership was not given to him, hence for wreaking vengeance, this present case has been instituted.
It is lastly submitted that there is no receipt of Rs.26,00,000/- cash having been handed over to the petitioner nos. 4 & 5.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer as prayed for in this criminal miscellaneous petition be allowed.

5. The learned P.P. and the learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer as made in this criminal miscellaneous petition and relying upon the Judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Priti Saraf & Anr. vs. State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr, reported in (2021) 16 SCC 142

entities.text: Priti Saraf & Anr. vs. State (NCT of Delhi) & Anr, reported in (2021) 16 SCC 142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, it is submitted that in para-31 thereof, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has observed that whether the allegations in the complaint are otherwise correct or not has to be decided on the basis of the evidence to be led during the course of the trial and in the facts of that case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was of the view that on plain reading of a complaint, it cannot be said that the complaint does not disclose the commission of an offence. It is next submitted that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner nos. 5 &
6 of dishonestly inducing the complainant to deliver Rs.10,00,000/- to the petitioner no.6 and Rs.16,00,000/- to the petitioner no.5 by cheating the complainant that upon making such payment,
the dealership of the complainant will be restarted and billing of five tractors will be done on behalf of the petitioner no.1 -company but the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 have dishonestly misappropriated the said entrusted money, therefore both the offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code as well as under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code are made out against the petitioner nos. 5 &
6.

It is next submitted that the petitioner no.5 &
6 undisputedly being the employees of the petitioner no.1, so obviously they having committed the offence on behalf of the petitioner no.1 and the petitioner nos. 2 to 4 being the other officers associated with the management of petitioner no.1- company, each of them are squarely responsible for having committed the said offence in furtherance of their common intention.
Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit be dismissed.

6. Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials available in the record, this Court finds that there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner nos. 5 &
6 of having been entrusted with Rs.16,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- respectively by the complainant but there is no specific allegation against the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 having received the same on behalf of the petitioner no.1 nor there is any direct and specific allegation against the petitioner nos. 2, 3 & 4 of having done any overt act, in the alleged commission of the offence.

7. Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that even if the entire allegations made against the petitioners are considered to be true in their entirety, still no offence is made out against the petitioner nos. 1 to 4.
Therefore, the continuation of this criminal proceeding against them will amount to abuse of process of law.

sentences.text: So far as the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 are concerned, there is direct and specific allegation against the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 of having cheated and dishonestly induced the complainant in furtherance of common intention, to part with and deliver Rs.16,00,000/- and Rs.10,00,000/- respectively and there is direct and specific allegation against them of dishonestly misappropriating the same.

Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that in view of the settled principle of law that a High Court in exercise of its power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot enter into a mini trial and cannot appreciate the evidence of the particular case as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. vs. Akhil Sharda & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw SC 594 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India reiterated the settled principle of law that no mini trial can be conducted by the High Court in exercise of its power under Section 482 Cr.P.C, the relevant portion of which reads as under :-
"

entities.text: State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr. vs. Akhil Sharda & Ors. reported in 2022 LiveLaw SC 594
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Having gone through the impugned judgment and order passed by the High court has set aside the criminal proceedings in exercise of powers under Section 482 CrPC,
it appears that the High Court has virtually conducted a mini trial, which as such is not permissible at this stage and while deciding the application under Section 482CrPC.

As observed and held by this court in a catena of decisions, no mini trial can be conducted by the High Court in exercise of power under Section 482CrPC,
jurisdiction and at the stage of deciding the application under Section 482CrPC, the High Court cannot get into appreciation of evidence of the particular case being considering.
(Emphasis supplied)

And also in view of the settled principle of law that in exercise of the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. the genuine prosecution cannot be stifled with, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Monica Kumar (Dr. )and Another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others reported in (2008) 8 SCC 781, this Court is of the considered view that in view of the fact that the offences punishable under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code is prima facie made out against the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 if the allegations made against them are considered to be true in their entirety.

entities.text: Monica Kumar (Dr. )and Another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and others reported in (2008) 8 SCC 781
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, this is not a fit case where the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 03.06.2023, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Dhanbad in Complaint Case No. 6913 of 2022 whereby and where under the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offence punishable under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioners and directed for issuance of summons against them be quashed and set aside so far as the petitioner nos. 5 & 6 are concerned.
9.

In view of the discussions made above, the entire criminal proceeding including the order dated 03.06.2023, passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate -1st Class, Dhanbad in Complaint Case No.
6913 of 2022 whereby and where under the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offence punishable under Section 406/34 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioners and directed for issuance of summons against them, is quashed and set aside qua the petitioner nos. 1 to 4 only.
10. This criminal miscellaneous petition is allowed to the aforesaid extent only.
